az_pinhead_wall.blurb: Pinhead Wall is a fin of rock beside the lower Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, close to Tucson, within the Hairpin Turn area. Most of its 21 lines are bolted sport routes with a handful of trad lines, running from an easy 5.7 up into the 5.12s, with the bulk landing in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Established climbing is on the narrow west face and the north face, and the north side stays shady enough to climb through much of the year. The stone is mostly sound but can be loose or crumbly in spots, so belayers should wear helmets. Bees have been reported in the wider area.
az_pinhead_wall.parking_note: Pull off at the roadside parking just before the sharp hairpin turn on the Catalina Highway, about half a mile up from the bottom, beside the national forest sign.
az_pinhead_wall.approach: Cross the road and follow the wash uphill until it bends sharply to the right; the wall sits directly above you at that point.

az_egg_the.blurb: The Egg is a granite boulder cluster within the Beardsley boulder pile in north Phoenix, a short distance south of the main bouldering hillside near the end of 20th Street. All 21 problems are bouldering, spread widely: a few very easy lines, a solid group in the middle grades around V4 and V5, and a handful of hard problems reaching double digits. Beardsley granite is coarse and weathered, and grades are old-school, so problems can feel stiff for their number. Bring a pad.

az_railroad_wall.blurb: Railroad Wall is a bouldering wall on the Drysdale Trail, part of the Lake Mary area near Flagstaff at roughly 7,000 feet. It holds 21 problems, mostly very easy to easy with a handful stretching to about V3, which makes it one of the friendlier walls along the trail. The trail links several boulder walls over about half a mile, with views toward Lower Lake Mary. Landings are a concern, so bring pads and good spotters. Grades are rough guesses. Park considerately and keep the dirt road clear, since forest staff pass through often.

az_cemetery_the.blurb: The Cemetery is a bouldering area in the Superstition Mountains east of Phoenix. Its 21 problems range from an easy warm-up up to double-digit difficulty, with a thick middle of V3 to V7 problems and a few highballs with flat, clear landings. The area is laid out as a warm-up gallery of boulders near the entrance, with trails leading deeper to a wall that encloses the far side. The Superstition volcanic rock can be loose or have portable holds, so test holds. Bolting is illegal in the Superstition Wilderness.

az_little_england_wall.blurb: Little England Wall is a modest welded-tuff wall in Queen Creek Canyon, near US-60 east of Phoenix and behind the Atlantis area. About twenty routes and one boulder problem, mostly trad, with a few sport lines; most grades are easy to moderate, roughly 5.4 to 5.10, which suits newer leaders. You walk up the Atlantis canyon to a dam, climb over it, and follow a cabled trail in the wash to the base, about ten minutes once in the canyon.

az_island_facelift_area_the.blurb: The Island is a small cluster of granite boulders beside a dirt parking lot with toilets, on Senator's Highway in the Groom Creek area south of Prescott, at around 6,000 feet. All 21 problems are bouldering. Roughly half are very easy, a few sit in the middle grades, and a handful reach V8 and above, so beginners and hard climbers both get something. The boulders are easy to spot between the lot and the road. It makes a quick stop, and the larger Groom Creek boulder fields, set among ponderosa pines, are a short distance away.

az_bowling_alley_main_wall.blurb: The Main Wall is the steep centerpiece of the Bowling Alley section of the Farmhouse crag, near Sonoita in southern Arizona. Its 21 routes are all bolted sport lines aimed at strong climbers: a single 5.10, a few 5.11s and 5.12s, and a big group at 5.13 plus some 5.14. The wall faces north and stays shaded all day, and the area has a long season. Respect red-tagged projects, and watch for loose rock in the gully beneath.
az_bowling_alley_main_wall.parking_note: Park in the turnoff on the north side of Highway 82 just east of the bridge; if full, use the next pullout past the bridge. Never block the ranch gate or the road leading to it.
az_bowling_alley_main_wall.approach: Walk up to the farmhouse area, take the left fork at the trail split, round the Prow's west side past the gully, and continue to the wall, which sits above a broad ledge.

_conflicts.az_egg_the: Stored parking is the Lone Cactus Road dead-end lot, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/119455338/the-egg says to park on the street by the boulder (near E Monona Dr / N 20th St); https://www.mountainproject.com/area/119455323/beardsley-bouldering has it about a quarter mile south of Lone Cactus parking. That page also lists V0- to V10 while its text says up to V8.
_conflicts.az_bowling_alley_main_wall: Stored rock is sandstone, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/109590816/the-farmhouse describes chert-rich high quality rock (Farmhouse crag generally described as limestone/chert).
